newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia seen paying premium at Wed T-bill auctions.
newsitem.headline: Russia seen paying premium at Wed T-bill auctions.

text.p: The Russian Finance Ministry may pay a small premium at Wednesday's government paper auctions as prices and demand have fallen over the last three trading sessions, dealers said on Tuesday.
* 2.10 trln rbls in interest and 3.30 trln rbls in repayment on OFZ bond (series 24004)
* Average yield rose to 25.6 pct from 25.1 on Monday
* Turnover rose to 4.9 bln rbls from 3.6 bln rbls
* The Central Bank did not intervene on the market

Dealers forecast the average yield on the T-bill, maturing on April 1, 1998 would be in the 26.40-27.20 percent. Series 23004 bills, maturing on April 8, 1998, the closest maturity date to the new issue on Tuesday closed at 83.50 to yield 25.67 percent.

Dealers forecast the average price on the bond issue, maturing on May 26, 1999, to be 97.51-98.71 percent. Series 24012 bonds, maturing on April 28, 1999, the closest maturity date to the new issue, closed at 99.30 to yield 33.60 percent.

"At the auction of 308-day paper one can expect a premium," said Troika Dialog head of fixed income Robert Devane. "Of course, it will not be a big one, but it may reach 0.5 percentage points. The market is in the process of a local price fall, which is not over yet. Non-residents are waiting for a higher yield."
A fall in funds deposited for trade ahead of trading sessions over the last five days showed declining demand from both resident and non-resident operators.
Banks sent 1.5 trillion roubles into the trading system on May 27 compared to 3.1 trillion roubles on May 20.
